# Vulnerabilities govulncheck reports that this build accepts, one OSV ID per
# line. Anything not listed here fails the build.
#
# An entry is a claim that somebody looked at the advisory and decided it does
# not apply, and it has to say why. An entry with no reasoning is an entry
# nobody can re-check when the advisory changes — and an allowlist nobody
# re-checks is worse than no scanner, because it reads like the scan passed.
#
# Review these whenever the module is upgraded. Remove an entry the moment a
# fixed version exists; the reason for keeping one is always "there is no fix",
# never "the fix is inconvenient".

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GO-2026-4887 — Moby: AuthZ plugin bypass with oversized request bodies
# GO-2026-4883 — Moby: off-by-one in plugin privilege validation
#
# Both are vulnerabilities in the Moby **daemon**. Pando imports
# github.com/docker/docker as a client library — it speaks to a daemon, it does
# not contain one — and neither the authorization-plugin path nor the plugin
# privilege path exists in the client.
#
# govulncheck reports them as called because the advisories name the whole
# module rather than specific symbols, so every trace it prints resolves to
# something like `docker.init calls filters.init`. That is module-level
# matching, not reachability.
#
# Neither has a fixed version (`Fixed in: N/A`), so there is no upgrade to take.
# The daemon these advisories are about is the host's own Docker installation
# and is patched by patching Docker, which is outside what Pando ships.
#
# Remove both when github.com/docker/docker publishes a fixed release.
# Last reviewed: 2026-09-14, against github.com/docker/docker v28.5.2.
GO-2026-4887
GO-2026-4883

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dependabot raises four more against the same module. They are recorded here
# rather than only in the Security tab, because a dismissal whose reasoning
# lives in a web UI is one nobody re-reads when the advisory changes. They are
# comments rather than entries: govulncheck does not report any of them as
# called, so scripts/check-vulns.py stays green without them and listing them
# would only produce "on the allowlist but not reported" notices.
#
#   GHSA-rg2x-37c3-w2rh  high    `docker cp` race redirects a bind mount to a
#            GO-2026-5617         host path
#   GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5  medium  `docker cp` race creates empty files at
#            GO-2026-5668         arbitrary host paths
#   GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r  high    PUT /containers/{id}/archive runs the
#            GO-2026-5746         container's decompression binary on the host
#   GHSA-pxq6-2prw-chj9  medium  off-by-one in plugin privilege validation
#            GO-2026-4883         — the entry above, under its other number
#
# All four are daemon code: the first three are the `docker cp` mount setup in
# the daemon's archive handling, the fourth is plugin installation. None of it
# is in the binary. `go list -deps ./internal/adapter/runtime/docker` resolves
# to exactly three things under that module — api/…, client, and pkg/stdcopy —
# and no daemon/… or plugin/… package at all.
#
# The exposure these advisories describe belongs to the host's own Docker
# installation, which is patched by patching Docker. Pando is one of the clients
# talking to it.
#
# github.com/docker/docker has no fixed release and will not get one: the module
# stops at v28.5.2+incompatible, and Moby's maintained line is the split-out
# github.com/moby/moby/api and github.com/moby/moby/client modules, which these
# advisories do not name. Those are already in the module graph, pulled in by
# testcontainers-go. Porting the runtime adapter onto them is what actually
# removes this dependency; it is a real port rather than a rename, because the
# client's surface moved to options and result structs. Tracked in issue #26.
#
# Dismissed on GitHub as "not used", each comment pointing back here.
# Last reviewed: 2026-09-14, against github.com/docker/docker v28.5.2.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GO-2026-5932 — golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is unmaintained and unsafe
#
# Not an entry, because it does not need one: govulncheck reports it as not
# called and the build stays green. Written down because Scorecard's
# Vulnerabilities check lists it next to the Moby ones, and the next person to
# read that list should not have to work this out again.
#
# `go mod why golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp` answers "main module does not need
# package". The advisory names the whole golang.org/x/crypto module, which is
# required for other packages; the openpgp package inside it is not linked.
# Pando's OpenPGP comes from github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto/openpgp by way of
# go-git — which is the maintained fork the advisory tells people to move to.
#
# Nothing to do unless `go list -deps ./cmd/pando` starts naming it.
